title: The Eusébio de Queirós Law
summary: Law No. 581 of 4 September 1850, passed by the Empire of Brazil under Pedro II and named for the Minister of Justice who carried it, abolished the international slave trade to Brazil. It re-enacted a law of 7 November 1831 that had never been enforced, and it was enforced. The government resented the British pressure that produced it — the seizures under the Aberdeen Act — and passed it anyway. Slavery itself stood for another thirty-eight years.
